# Popconfirm

Popconfirm: a lightweight confirmation that pops up next to its trigger, for actions with a small impact that
still need confirming (such as removing one access grant). Irreversible actions such as deleting an object or
clearing data use useConfirmDanger.

**Interaction**: when it opens, focus moves to "Cancel" (pressing `Enter` does not confirm by accident); `Tab`
moves between "Cancel" and "Confirm", and `Enter` / `Space` trigger them; `Esc` closes it. After confirming,
cancelling or closing with `Esc`, focus returns to the trigger.

**Category**: Feedback · **Common uses**: Removing a member, revoking access, deleting a draft row

## Import

```ts
import { Popconfirm } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

For actions with a small impact that still need confirmation; irreversible deletions use useConfirmDanger.

```tsx
import { Button, Popconfirm } from 'vellum-ui'

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Popconfirm
      title="Remove this grant?"
      description='Alex Morgan will no longer have access to "Website redesign / Mockups".'
      okText="Remove"
      okTone="danger"
      onConfirm={() => {}}
    >
      <Button>Remove</Button>
    </Popconfirm>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | The question, such as "Remove this member?". | — | Yes |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | Explanation below the question: what will happen. | — | No |
| `okText` | `ReactNode` | Text of the confirm button; the built-in text ("OK") by default. | — | No |
| `okTone` | `'danger'` | Semantic color of the confirm button: `danger` for destructive actions. | — | No |
| `onConfirm` | `() => void` | Called when the user confirms. When it returns a promise, the confirm button shows a loading indicator and the popup stays open until the promise settles. | — | No |
| `onCancel` | `() => void` | Called when the user cancels with the Cancel button. | — | No |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | The trigger: one element that accepts events and a ref, usually a Button or a LinkButton. | — | No |

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.
